turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, Doctor. Mrs Pillay is in for her routine review. Blood pressure is one hundred and forty-six over eighty-eight, pulse seventy-six. On the script I've got amlodipine five milligrams once a day, and atorvastatin twenty milligrams at night.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks, Sister. Stay close, I might need you. Mrs Pillay, come through. How are you keeping?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Good morning, Doctor. I am here for my routine check, thank you. This is my daughter, Priya. I hope it is acceptable that she sits in with me.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hello, Doctor. I'll try not to interrupt. She wanted company, that's all.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're welcome. Right, let me think back. Last time we were keeping an eye on your high blood pressure and the high cholesterol. How have things been on your side?
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): I have been quite well in myself, despite the blood pressure and the cholesterol. There is, however, something I ought to tell you, and I do apologise.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please don't apologise. I'm listening.

[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): I stopped the cholesterol tablet, the atorvastatin. I stopped it in March... well, actually, I nearly said February, but no, it was March, just after my birthday. I had read an article online about statins and one's memory, and it frightened me rather badly.
[SEG0009] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She only told me weeks afterwards. I said phone the rooms, Mom.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm not going to scold you. People read things and they worry, that's human. Let me just work through it. Did you get any muscle aches, or was it purely the article?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Purely the article, Doctor. I had no muscle pain whatsoever. I felt perfectly fine whilst I was taking it.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain since you stopped?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No, none at all.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): And shortness of breath?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No, I would not say so.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Dizziness? Headaches?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No dizziness. I do get a mild headache now and again. I have had that for years, though, and it settles if I sit quietly. It is nothing new.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Noted. And the blood pressure tablet, the amlodipine. Are you still taking that one?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. I take it every day... well, actually, I must be frank. I take it every other day. I thought every day might be a little much.
[SEG0020] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, Sister, can I just jump in. You said five milligrams. The box in her cupboard says ten. I checked it yesterday.
[SEG0021] person_1 (NURSE): The file and the last script both say five milligrams once daily. I haven't seen the box, so I can only read what's written.
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): I am terribly sorry. I cannot recall the strength with any confidence. The packet is at home.

[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): So the script says five and the box apparently says ten, and we are not going to invent an answer. Bring the packet next time and we'll line it up. I'm leaving the dose blank in my mind for now.

[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): What I will say, thinking it through, is that one hundred and forty-six over eighty-eight is a touch higher than I would like, and taking the tablet only every other day may well be the reason. That is my working impression, not a firm diagnosis.
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): I understand. Shall I go back to taking it daily?
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, please. One tablet every morning, not every other day, and if you miss a day don't take two the next. Until we see the box, just use the tablets you already have.
[SEG0027] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mom, you were going on in the car about Dad's diabetes pills. Tell the doctor.

[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, thank you, Priya. My husband has diabetes and he takes metformin. I wondered whether I ought to take it too, but I have never taken a diabetes tablet. Someone at the chemist once mentioned one, and I never started it.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Metformin belongs to your husband, not to you. We don't share those out. Has anyone ever said that you yourself have diabetes?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. Never.

[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. I'll still ask for a glucose, because it has been a while and the test is simple, not because I suspect it. Let me list what I actually want: fasting lipids, an ALT for the liver given the statin question, creatinine and electrolytes with the blood pressure tablet, and that fasting glucose.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): That is very clear. I appreciate you explaining it properly.
[SEG0033] person_1 (NURSE): Thursday morning is open at the lab if you'd like me to book her in, Doctor.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please, Sister. Book the fasting bloods for Thursday: lipid profile, ALT, creatinine, electrolytes, and a fasting glucose.
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): Thursday is perfectly suitable. Do I need to fast?
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. Nothing but water from about ten the night before, and aim to be at the lab before nine. You may take the amlodipine that morning with water.
[SEG0037] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll get her there. Dad was going to lend the car, then he remembered the chemist... ag, I'll sort a lift. Not your problem, sorry.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): It's no trouble. Whilst I think of it, any medicine that has ever disagreed with you? Allergies?
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): None at all, Doctor. I have never had an allergy to a medicine.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): And do you smoke, or take a drink?
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): I have never smoked. I have one small glass of wine on a Sunday, with lunch. We stay in Rondebosch, just my husband and myself.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you manage any walking, or is the day mostly indoors?
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): I walk to the shops most mornings. It is about twenty minutes. I enjoy it, except when the robot by the mall is out and the traffic gets rather hectic.

[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's plenty. I'm not restarting the atorvastatin today. In a month, once these bloods are back, we'll look at the cholesterol together and decide. If the level is high I would lean towards restarting it, but that is only a maybe, not a script I'm writing now.
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): I am relieved you are not angry with me. I was quite anxious about coming to tell you.

[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'd much rather you phone the rooms before you stop anything else. An article online doesn't know your file. And please bring the amlodipine box, so we can settle whether it is five or ten.
[SEG0047] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll put it in her handbag the night before. Otherwise it stays in the cupboard, and then we're none the wiser.
[SEG0048] person_3 (PATIENT): I shall bring the packet, and I shall take the blood pressure tablet every morning, as you have advised. Thank you kindly for your patience, Doctor.

[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back in a month. Reception can book that visit on your way out, and we'll revisit the statin and check the pressure again. Sister, may I have the lab form before they go.
